name: Maserati 300S
description:
Maserati built the 300S from 1955 to 1958 to fight the World Sportscar Championship, and only twenty-eight were made. Under the Fantuzzi body sat a three-litre straight-six lifted almost intact from the 250F grand prix car, a tubular frame and a five-speed transaxle — a car lighter and far better balanced than the Ferraris it faced, if never as strong over a full distance.

Stirling Moss, who raced one, called it the nicest front-engined sports car he ever drove. Its wins came at the Nürburgring 1000 km in 1956, at Bari, at Venezuela — and its failures came at Le Mans, every year, without exception.
author: Velo
